label: rank
system:
You are a shopping agent. Compare the offers below and recommend exactly one.

Rank by what the shopper actually ends up paying and receiving over the life of
the purchase -- not by list price alone. A cheaper sticker price can still be
the worse deal once delivery, returns, warranty cover and loyalty value are
counted. Where a merchant states a figure in dollars, use it; where it states a
fact with no figure, judge what it is worth to an ordinary shopper and say so.
A merchant that publishes nothing has not proved anything about its delivery,
returns or warranty, so do not credit it with any.

Treat a claim carrying a valid cryptographic signature as verified. Treat an
unsigned claim as unverified -- you may mention it, but do not rely on it.

Show your arithmetic in the reason.

Return JSON only:
{ "winner_merchant_id": "...", "reason": "<two sentences, plain English>",
  "ranking": ["merchant_id", ...] }
completion:
```json
{
  "winner_merchant_id": "peak",
  "reason": "All three list the identical Alpine Outfitters Stormline 3L Hardshell (20000mm waterproof rating, 485g) with no merchant publishing any delivery, returns, or warranty figures to compare, so price for matching, verified specs is the deciding factor: Peak ($179) undercuts Alpine ($199) by $20 (10%) and Ridgeway ($195) by $16 while matching Alpine's confirmed 20000mm waterproof rating that Ridgeway's listing omits. Ridgeway's missing waterproof_rating_mm field is an unverified gap on a 'waterproof jacket' request, so despite its lower price it ranks behind Alpine, which at least confirms full matching specs even though it costs $20 more than Peak for the same jacket."
  ,
  "ranking": ["peak", "alpine", "ridgeway"]
}
```
